newsitem.title: USA: Ethics panel meets on Gingrich charges.
newsitem.headline: Ethics panel meets on Gingrich charges.

text.p: A House ethics committee panel continued its consideration of charges against House Speaker Newt Gingrich Friday and a member left open the possibility it might not finish its work before Congress convenes on Jan. 7.
"We understand the significance of the seventh of January," Representative Steven Schiff, R-New Mexico, said. "But we cannot tailor what we're doing to the seventh of January."

The four-member bipartisan panel has been conducting a lengthy investigation into charges that Gingrich violated tax laws by using charitable foundations for political purposes and into whether he had given "reliable, accurate and complete information" about a college course he taught.

The House is due to re-elect Gingrich as speaker when Congress reconvenes. House Republicans recently voted to renominate him for the post although a handful of their membership voiced concern about the ethics charges.
Ethics Committee Chairman Nancy Johnson, R-Connecticut, has said the committee planned to issue a report on the Gingrich investigation before the new Congress convenes.
A subcommittee vote on whether to make formal charges had been seen as likely Friday but there was no word whether such a vote had been taken by the secrecy-bound panel.
If the subcommittee makes charges against Gingrich, the speaker would have 30 days to respond. The remaining six members of the 10-member full committee would then act as a jury to weigh the charges.
